title: 'Grantchester' Ends After 11 Seasons as Rishi Nair's Indian-Heritage Vicar Delivers Final Sermon
excerpt: The beloved PBS Masterpiece mystery series wraps with its final season set in 1963, centering Alphy Kottaram's crisis of faith and quest for identity.
body:
• PBS Masterpiece mystery series 'Grantchester' concludes its 11-season, 75-episode run with a finale centering Rishi Nair's character, Alphy Kottaram — a crime-solving vicar of Indian heritage set in 1963 England.
  • The final season follows Alphy's crisis of faith after meeting his birth mother, Mira, who left him on the doorstep of a foundling home run by a white reverend.
  • Nair, a British actor of Indian descent, joined the series in Season 9 and became the show's third vicar lead after James Norton and Tom Brittney.
  • Executive producer Daisy Coulam said the central question of the final season is: "Where do we find belonging and where do we find meaning?"

A Farewell to Grantchester

After 11 seasons, 75 episodes, and three handsome vicars, PBS Masterpiece's 'Grantchester' is saying goodbye. The long-running British mystery series aired its final episodes set in 1963, with Rishi Nair's Alphy Kottaram — the show's first Indian-heritage lead — delivering the last sermon.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=MtSJw2hx4-Q

Nair, who joined 'Grantchester' during its ninth season, said the decision to end the show was "bittersweet" but felt right. "The show's in a really good place, and sometimes going out on a high is the smart move," he told TV Insider.

Alphy's Crisis of Identity

The final season picks up after the Season 10 cliffhanger, in which Alphy met his birth mother, Mira, played by Nimmi Harasgama. The child of Indian parents, Alphy was raised in an orphanage run by a white reverend after his mother left him on the doorstep. Reconnecting with Mira forces him to confront questions about his heritage, his faith, and whether the church was ever truly his home.

https://x.com/Variety/status/2084070320953299218

"He's always felt that he is a part of the church, and suddenly finding his mother, it makes him question everything. Where do we find belonging and where do we find meaning?"

— Daisy Coulam, Executive Producer and Head Writer

"Alphy's one of those people who always presents himself as a very glass-half-full, positive person," Nair said. "That mindset is tested because he loses his faith, and that's kind of what his whole life is about."

The finale takes a dark turn when a fugitive, Dexter Sutton, shoots Detective Inspector Geordie Keating, played by Robson Green. The crisis pushes Alphy over the edge. "At that point, Alphy's lost his faith in God," Nair explained. "I was surprised at how dark Alphy went, but I was also really excited by it."

Indian Representation on British Television

Nair's casting as the third vicar in 'Grantchester' was a quiet milestone for South Asian representation in British period drama — a genre that has historically centered white characters. His character's storyline directly engaged with questions of race, belonging, and the immigrant experience in 1960s England, themes that resonated with British Asian viewers and the Indian diaspora worldwide.

The show's writers wove Alphy's Indian identity into the fabric of the narrative rather than treating it as a sidebar. His struggle to reconcile his upbringing in a white institution with his Indian roots mirrors a tension familiar to many second-generation diaspora viewers.

The Legacy

'Grantchester,' adapted from James Runcie's novels about a vicar and a detective solving crimes in a picturesque English village, premiered on PBS in January 2015. It became one of Masterpiece's most reliable performers, surviving two lead-actor transitions — from James Norton to Tom Brittney to Nair — while maintaining its audience.

For Coulam, who has been with the show for over a quarter of her lifetime, letting go was emotional. "I'm going to get emotional," she told TV Insider. "We got the green light for 'Grantchester' when I was in Costa Rica on honeymoon."

Nair, for his part, is leaving with gratitude. "In any field, it's the people that make your experience there, and the people at 'Grantchester' really are like a family."
nri_angle: Rishi Nair's casting as the first Indian-heritage lead in a major British period drama represented a milestone for South Asian representation on Western television.
